usage.callShape: GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/flightaware/flights/{fa_flight_id}/position (path param is a FlightAware fa_flight_id, e.g. UAL237-1779611729-fa-1059p)
usage.outputShape: On success: body with live position fields (lat/lon/altitude/groundspeed/heading) for the given flight. On failure: body.success=false, body.error (FlightAware error string). The tested example returned body.error with reason NO_DATA because the example fa_flight_id was stale.
quirks: The path segment is a FlightAware fa_flight_id (a time-encoded identifier like UAL237-1779611729-fa-1059p), NOT a plain flight number like UAL237. You must first obtain a CURRENT fa_flight_id from the search endpoint (GET /api/flightaware/flights/search?query=-idents UAL237) before calling this — IDs encode a timestamp and expire as the flight ages out of FlightAware's data window.

The hardcoded registry example fa_flight_id (UAL237-1779611729-fa-1059p) is now stale: it returns HTTP 400 with body.error reason NO_DATA. This is upstream FlightAware 'no data', not a broken route — the endpoint paid and responded correctly.

Errors are returned as body.success=false + body.error (still HTTP 400) rather than a thrown gateway error; you still get charged $0.02 even on a NO_DATA result, so always source a live fa_flight_id first.
usage.guide: Pay-per-call x402 ($0.02 on Base USDC, no API key). This returns the live position/track point for a single flight identified by a FlightAware fa_flight_id in the URL path. Do NOT use a plain flight number — first call the sibling search endpoint (GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/flightaware/flights/search?query=-idents UAL237) to get a current fa_flight_id from body.flights[].fa_flight_id, then call GET /api/flightaware/flights/{fa_flight_id}/position. Read position data from the response body on success; on failure check body.success and body.error. Note you are charged even when FlightAware returns NO_DATA for a stale/expired identifier.
